content.comment_body: I have a similar issue when installing the setup.bin file on a Linux system (Chromebook with Crouton Trusty). Running the installation command for [product_name] results in the following output, whether using the 32-bit or 64-bit version: (xenial)[user_name]@localhost:~/Downloads$ ./setup32bit.bin Preparing to install... WARNING: /tmp does not have enough disk space! Switching to /home/[user_name] for installation base and temporary directory. Extracting the Java Runtime Environment (JRE) from the archive... Unpacking JRE... Extracting installation resources from the archive... Configuring installer for this system's environment... Launching installer... /home/[user_name]/install.dir.326/Linux/resource/jre/bin/java: 1: /home/[user_name]/install.dir.326/Linux/resource/jre/bin/java: ELF ...: not found /home/[user_name]/install.dir.326/Linux/resource/jre/bin/java: 2: /home/[user_name]/install.dir.326/Linux/resource/jre/bin/java: Syntax error: "(" unexpected (xenial)[user_name]@localhost:~/Downloads$ ./setup64bit.bin Preparing to install... WARNING: /tmp does not have enough disk space! Switching to /home/[user_name] for installation base and temporary directory. Extracting the JRE... Unpacking JRE... Extracting installation resources from the archive... Configuring installer for this system's environment... Launching installer... /home/[user_name]/install.dir.959/Linux/resource/jre/bin/java: 1: /home/[user_name]/install.dir.959/Linux/resource/jre/bin/java: Syntax error: end of file unexpected (expecting "") --- Split from install software on Linux Mint.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are confronted with critical installation failures when trying to run [company_name] software using the provided binary installer on a Linux distribution (Chromebook/Crouton Trusty). The process stops due to insufficient disk space warnings and unrecoverable Java runtime errors, preventing successful setup. Users expect reliable installation support in diverse Linux environments, suggesting current compatibility and error handling are insufficient.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that installing [company_name] software will work smoothly on commonly used Linux distributions, regardless of system architecture. The installer should manage system resources and environment variables robustly, without producing fatal errors.
